answer:
Let \(x\) be the distance of the foot from the wall, and \(y\) the height of the top of the ladder. Since the ladder has length \(5\),

\[
x^2+y^2=25.
\]

Differentiate with respect to time:

\[
2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0
\]

so

\[
\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt}.
\]

Given \(\frac{dx}{dt}=0.5\) m/s.

### When the foot is \(3\) m from the wall
Then

\[
x=3,\qquad y=\sqrt{25-9}=4.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{3}{4}(0.5)=-0.375\text{ m/s}.
\]

So the top is sliding down at

\[
\boxed{0.375\text{ m/s}\approx 0.38\text{ m/s}}.
\]

### When both ends move at the same speed
The foot’s speed is \(0.5\) m/s. The top’s downward speed is

\[
-\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{x}{y}(0.5).
\]

Set this equal to \(0.5\):

\[
\frac{x}{y}(0.5)=0.5 \implies x=y.
\]

Using \(x^2+y^2=25\):

\[
2x^2=25 \implies x=y=\frac{5}{\sqrt2}.
\]

So both ends have the same speed when the foot is

\[
\boxed{x=\frac{5}{\sqrt2}\approx 3.54\text{ m from the wall}}
\]

and the top is at the same height. At that instant both speeds are \(0.5\) m/s.

If time starts when the foot is at the wall, this occurs at

\[
t=\frac{x}{0.5}=\frac{5/\sqrt2}{0.5}=5\sqrt2\approx 7.07\text{ s}.
\]

If time starts when the foot is \(3\) m from the wall, it occurs after

\[
\frac{\frac{5}{\sqrt2}-3}{0.5}
=5\sqrt2-6\approx 1.07\text{ s}.
\]

### Check
At \(x=y\), we have \(\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{dx}{dt}\), so the top and foot have equal speed magnitudes. Also,

\[
x\frac{dx}{dt}+y\frac{dy}{dt}
=x(0.5)+x(-0.5)=0,
\]

which agrees with the constant ladder length condition.
